title: Reuse-Aware Compilation for Zoned Quantum Architectures Based on Neutral Atoms
problem: Neutral-atom quantum computers use heterogeneous zoned architectures (storage, entangling, readout zones), and compiling quantum circuits for them requires efficiently managing qubit movement between zones to minimize fidelity-degrading data movement overhead.
motivation: Zoned architectures significantly improve computation fidelity by shielding idling qubits from noise, but the increased structural complexity makes efficient compilation much harder than for monolithic single-zone architectures.
method: ZAC (Zoned Architecture Compiler) optimizes quantum circuits for zoned quantum computers by keeping qubits in the entanglement zone when they'll be used there immediately, avoiding wasteful round-trips to and from storage. It also predicts future operations to decide optimal qubit placement and schedules operations more efficiently for zone-specific constraints using ZAIR, an intermediate representation that tracks which zone each qubit needs to be in. The compiler uses a flexible specification language to adapt to different zoned quantum architectures. On real circuits, this approach achieves 22x better signal quality (fidelity) compared to monolithic (non-zoned) quantum computers.
key_novelty: The key insight is that keeping qubits in the entanglement zone when they're about to be used there cuts out wasteful movement between zones, which is the primary source of signal quality loss in zoned quantum computers.
contributions: ZAC compiler with reuse-aware scheduling that retains qubits in the entanglement zone across consecutive entangling gates
ZAIR intermediate representation for flexible specification of diverse zoned neutral-atom architectures
Novel data placement and instruction scheduling strategies tailored to multi-zone architectures
22x fidelity improvement over monolithic architectures; within 10% of ideal solution on average

metrics.accuracy: 22x fidelity improvement over monolithic architectures; 10% fidelity gap from ideal on average

limitations: ZAC achieves only within 10% of the ideal optimal fidelity on average, indicating room for improvement in qubit placement and scheduling optimality.
primary_theme: reuse-aware compilation for zoned neutral-atom quantum architectures
